narrative: The market is currently navigating a 'clearing event' centered on the US midterm elections and a significant reassessment of the AI trade. Tech stocks have entered correction territory as investors shift from AI hype to execution-focused scrutiny, highlighted by Apple's revenue miss in China. Simultaneously, crude oil has plunged on reports of potential US-Iran diplomacy, easing immediate geopolitical risk premiums. While mega-cap tech faces liquidity headwinds, some analysts expect a broader market rally once election uncertainty is resolved.

Nasdaq.why: The index entered correction territory, dropping 10% from its October high as hedge funds deleverage tech holdings and AI monetization doubts grow, according to Howard Marks and Bloomberg anchors.

S&P 500.why: Mike Wilson forecasts a potential 9% pullback around the midterms before a rally to 8,000, while lower oil prices are seen buoying broader sentiment beyond tech.

Gold.why: Prices broke below the key $4,000 technical level and are showing an unusual correlation with falling tech stocks during de-grossing, according to Anthony Stephens.

Oil.why: Brent and WTI fell over 6% following reports that Donald Trump is seeking diplomacy with Iran to avoid military strikes and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
